assessment_summary: The proof's Lemma 1 attempts to show that the minimum degree of the graph is strictly greater than alpha*n. After assuming for contradiction that there exists a vertex with degree <= alpha*n, the proof correctly deduces that this would imply alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n (Step 0051). However, in Step 0052, it falsely claims that this inequality is violated for any fixed alpha > 0 and sufficiently large n. In reality, for any alpha < 1/2 (which was established earlier in the proof), the inequality alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n is satisfied (not violated) for sufficiently large n. Thus, no contradiction is reached, and Lemma 1 is unproven (and in fact, false, as an isolated vertex alongside a large clique is a counterexample).
